chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Fitrah (alms of fitr), how much should be paid for each head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins? He said, 'A sa' with the sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah, the alms of fitr paid at the end of Ramadan or upon death
key_terms.بِصَاعِ النَّبِيِّ: According to the measure of the Prophet
key_terms.صَاع: Sa', a traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed amount and measure for Fitrah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the obligatory alms of Fitrah is one Sa' per person, explicitly linking the measurement to the Prophet's standard to ensure continuity in religious practice. It specifically lists wheat, barley, dates, and raisins as the primary staples, reflecting the agricultural context of Medina and establishing a fixed, tangible obligation for the poor during Eid al-Fitr. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophetic measure (Sa' al-Nabi) rather than local variations, ensuring uniformity in charitable distribution.
